correctness.rationale: Exact heat-kernel shortest-path coefficients plus integrable matrix-semigroup Taylor remainder yield positive covariance leading terms. Division by positive diagonal coefficients proves the sharp Pearson rate and coefficient. Nearest-source intersection iff zero exponent; factorial strict log-convexity and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz prove perfect-limit classification. The exact rational independent Lyapunov recurrence verifies all leading covariance/variance coefficients for 46 ordered diagonal/unordered pair entries on four weighted graphs; this is supporting evidence, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Localized environmental forcing and dispersal-induced population synchrony are ecological modeling targets documented in the cited metapopulation literature. The proposed integer decay exponent measures how far two habitat fluctuations are from their common shock sources; the exact weighted shortest-path coefficient and zero/perfect synchrony classification provide a reusable interpretation of graph heterogeneity. A single noise source yields surprising distance-only limiting correlations and the ambient-noise/noncommuting migration limit delineates the practical mathematical boundary. This is not a routine two-patch computation or an arbitrary graph slice, though it is a linearized theoretical model.
